headline: Fed hike bets after hot CPI push the dollar to a 19-month high; euro breaks 1.11, yen near 160
summary: The dollar index rose about 0.65% to near 102.9, its highest since April 2025, as markets digested the third hot core CPI and calls from Waller and Logan for faster Fed hikes, putting December odds near 90% with about 12% for 50bp. The franc, euro and yen fell most, with the euro at its lowest since May 2025, while the won, rupee and Taiwan dollar held firm on equity inflows and steady officials.
drivers: Fed repricing extends the dollar rally

Futures now price close to a 90% chance of a December hike and about 12% for 50bp after Waller floated a half-point move and Logan backed at least two more hikes, possibly back to back. The dollar index topped its October high of 102.94 and the franc fell about 1%, its worst day among majors.
Europe's own risks deepen the euro slide

The euro broke 1.11 and touched about 1.1082, its lowest since May 2025, as the ECB is priced only about 65% for a December hike against a fully priced Fed. French 10-year yields near 5% and Lagarde's early exit in February add a risk premium.

The Kospi rose 2.6% and the Taiex 3.6%, so the won firmed 3.9 to 1,333.6 and the Taiwan dollar edged up to 32.86 as foreign selling shrank to NT$0.8bn. The rupiah, ringgit and peso lost about 0.45–0.55% to the firmer dollar, the rupiah also hurt by an impeachment push against Indonesia's vice-president.
view: Still bullish for the next 1–2 weeks: the Fed is set to hike in December and may go faster, while the ECB, RBA, BoC and SNB are priced to do less, so I back the dollar against the euro, Aussie and loonie. I fade it only against the yen above 160, where Tokyo is likely to step in. A soft PPI on Nov 13 or a DXY close back below 102.0 would turn me neutral.
ideas: Hold the long from 1.4080–1.4100 as the Fed outpaces the BoC; for 1.4450, stop raised to 1.4150.
Hold the short from 1.1170–1.1190 after the break of 1.11; for 1.1000, stop cut to 1.1160.
Hold the sale from 0.6900–0.6920 with the RBA done; for 0.6750, stop cut to 0.6905.
review: The USD/CAD buy is about 155 pips in favour, the EUR/USD short about 80 and the AUD/USD sale about 65, so I trail all three stops. The USD/JPY short was stopped at 159.40 as the pair hit about 159.9; the USD/CHF and CNH/JPY ranges broke higher and are reset, and the other ranges held.

eurusd.note: Down about 0.6% to near 1.1101 after a low near 1.1082, the lowest since May 2025; the short is about 80 pips in favour.
eurusd.why: The dollar did most of the moving. Waller's case for a 50bp December hike and Logan's call for faster hikes lifted Fed pricing to about 90%, while the ECB is priced only about 65% for December after cheaper oil trimmed hike bets. Europe added its own drag: French 10-year yields near 5%, a shrinking French economy and Lagarde's early exit in February keep a risk premium on the euro.
eurusd.outlook: I hold the short for 1.1000, a round number and Rabobank's three-month forecast, with the stop cut to 1.1160: the pair is below its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages. A close above 1.1160 would show the break of 1.11 has failed.
eurusd.watch: US PPI (Nov 13), ECB speakers ahead of December, French bond spreads, Fed speakers.

view.call: Short from 1.1170–1.1190; Fed outpaces the ECB.

gbpusd.note: Down about 0.5% to near 1.3280, at the bottom of my range and near a two-week low.
gbpusd.why: The dollar did the moving. The pound has less rate support than a week ago because the BoE's first hike in three years is already priced, while US hike odds keep rising. Brent rose about 1.4% on the day, a mild drag for an energy importer, and traders stayed cautious before Thursday's Q3 GDP, forecast at 0.7% quarter on quarter.
gbpusd.outlook: I shift the range down to 1.3250–1.3450: BoE hike pricing supports dips, but the Fed keeps the upside capped. A close below 1.3250, especially after a weak GDP print, would open 1.3150, the October low.
gbpusd.watch: UK Q3 GDP (Nov 12), US PPI (Nov 13), BoE speakers, UK CPI next week.

view.call: 1.3250–1.3450; UK GDP decides the next leg.

audusd.note: Down about 0.3% to near 0.6844, a seven-month low, after breaking 0.6855 support; the sale is about 65 pips in favour.
audusd.why: Both sides moved. The Fed repricing lifted the dollar, while the Aussie lacks rate support: the RBA's 6–3 hike to 4.85% on Nov 3 dropped its tightening bias, and four-year-low consumer sentiment plus weak business conditions have traders ruling out a December move. The break of 0.6855 triggered stop-loss selling toward the new low.
audusd.outlook: I hold the sale for 0.6750, the next support, and cut the stop to 0.6905: the RBA looks done while the Fed is still hiking. A hot Australian jobs report on Nov 19 and a close above 0.6905 would end the call.
audusd.watch: Australia jobs (Nov 19), monthly CPI (Nov 25), China data, US PPI (Nov 13).

view.call: Sale from 0.6900–0.6920; RBA done, Fed hiking.

usdjpy.note: Up about 0.7% to near 159.8 after touching about 159.9, the yen's weakest since early September; the short was stopped at 159.40.
usdjpy.why: The dollar did the moving. Higher odds of a faster Fed path widened the rate gap again and revived carry trades, pushing the pair through its 100-day average near 159.0. The yen got no help from the BoJ's hawkish summary of opinions, and the US cash bond market was shut for Veterans Day, so the move came through futures and FX alone.
usdjpy.outlook: I close the short at its stop and would sell again only at 160.00–160.30, where intervention risk jumps; Japan spent a record ¥7.98tn in one day in July. Target 157.80, stop 161.00; a close above 161 would show Tokyo is standing aside.
usdjpy.watch: Tokyo comments near 160, Japan Q3 GDP next week, US PPI (Nov 13), BoJ speakers.

usdchf.note: Up about 0.85% to near 0.8322 after hitting about 0.8335, a four-week high; the franc was the weakest major.
usdchf.why: The dollar did the moving, and the franc suffered most from the rate gap. The SNB holds at 0% and is not expected to hike soon even with Swiss inflation at 1.5%, so a Fed heading higher makes the franc a funding currency again. Calm equity markets kept haven demand low, and the break above 0.8295–0.8313 resistance drew in trend buyers.
usdchf.outlook: The 0.8130–0.8280 range is broken, so I reset it higher to 0.8250–0.8400 with an upward tilt: the rate gap favours the dollar, but the October high at 0.8395 and SNB intervention talk cap it. A close above 0.8400 would open a long.
usdchf.watch: US PPI (Nov 13), SNB comments, equity sentiment, Swiss inflation (early Dec).

usdcad.note: Up about 0.4% to near 1.4245, the loonie's weakest since mid-October; the buy is about 155 pips in favour.
usdcad.why: Mostly the dollar moved. Rising Fed odds widened the US-Canada rate gap, which had already moved in the dollar's favour after Canada's third straight monthly job loss and BoC minutes that showed no urgency to hike again in December. A 1.4% rebound in Brent gave the loonie only modest relief.
usdcad.outlook: I hold the buy and raise the target to 1.4450, the start of the April 2025 resistance zone, with the stop up to 1.4150: the Fed is hiking while the BoC waits. A close below 1.4150 would end the call; 1.4299, the October high, is the next test.
usdcad.watch: US PPI (Nov 13), Canada CPI (Nov 17), BoC speakers, oil and US-Iran headlines.

view.call: Long from 1.4080–1.4100; Fed hikes, BoC on hold.

usdcnh.note: Little changed near 6.674 offshore after the PBOC set its weakest fixing since Oct 22.
usdcnh.why: Beijing did the moving again. The PBOC fixed the midpoint at 6.7191, 336 pips weaker than the 6.6855 market estimate, after a 512-pip gap on Tuesday, signalling it wants the yuan's 5% rally to slow. A rise in the FX reserve ratio to 6% from 4% also drains offshore dollars, so the yuan barely reacted to the broad dollar rally.
usdcnh.outlook: I keep the 6.64–6.70 range: the PBOC leans against gains while exporters sell dollars on rallies. A close above 6.70 would show Beijing wants a weaker yuan.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings vs estimates, FX reserve ratio rise (Nov 15), China activity data.

view.call: 6.64–6.70; PBOC slows the yuan, exporters sell USD.

usdhkd.note: Steady near 7.844, close to the weak end of the 7.75–7.85 band.
usdhkd.why: Nothing local moved the pair. US rates stayed far above HIBOR and HKMA bill yields near 2.8–2.9%, so the carry gap that favours holding US dollars is unchanged and keeps the Hong Kong dollar near the weak side of its peg. The broad dollar rally had little effect because the peg limits moves.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in 7.83–7.85: the carry gap keeps it near 7.85, and only a jump in HIBOR or HKMA buying at 7.85 would pull it lower.
usdhkd.watch: HKMA operations at 7.85, HIBOR, US PPI (Nov 13).

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Up about 0.15% to near 1.2839; MAS's reference rate was 1.2819.
usdsgd.why: The dollar did the moving, but the Singapore dollar held up better than most. It was one of the few currencies the ringgit lost to on the day, as the MAS policy band keeps it on a gradual appreciating path and limits swings. That left it falling far less than the euro or franc as Fed hike bets rose.
usdsgd.outlook: I keep the 1.2740–1.2860 range: the MAS band supports the currency, but a Fed set to hike limits gains. A close above 1.2860 would open 1.2920.
usdsgd.watch: US PPI (Nov 13), Singapore final Q3 GDP, Asian tech-stock flows.

usdkrw.note: Won firmed 3.9 to 1,333.6 in Seoul despite the dollar rally; offshore it eased to about 1,338.6.
usdkrw.why: The won did the moving in Seoul. The pair opened up 6.0 at 1,343.5 on the US CPI, but offshore funds that had bought dollars at 1,350–1,360 cut those positions and added bets on a lower rate. The Kospi jumped 2.6% to about 5,375 on a chip rally, helping sentiment, before the stronger dollar trimmed the gain offshore.
usdkrw.outlook: I keep the 1,330–1,365 range: offshore positioning has turned won-positive, but a Fed set to hike limits gains. A Seoul close below 1,330 would open 1,315; above 1,365 would revive the long.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign Kospi flows, Korean authorities' comments, AI-chip sentiment, US PPI (Nov 13).

view.call: 1,330–1,365; offshore longs cut vs firm Fed.

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar edged up 0.5 cent to 32.86 in Taipei after hitting 32.968; offshore near 32.86.
usdtwd.why: Easing outflows and the central bank did the moving. The Taiex jumped 3.6% to 44,257, and foreign selling shrank to about NT$0.8bn on its tenth straight day, down from NT$34bn on Tuesday and over NT$830bn in total. The currency slid toward 33 early on the US CPI, but the central bank stepped in late and turnover fell to US$2.35bn as exporters waited.
usdtwd.outlook: I keep the 32.60–33.05 range: officials defend 33 and outflows are fading, but foreigners have not turned buyers. A close above 33.05 would show the defence has failed; a turn to foreign buying would open 32.60.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, central bank action, foreign index-futures shorts, US PPI (Nov 13).

usdmyr.note: Ringgit fell about 0.45% to 4.0710/0745 at the 6pm KL close, from 4.0540/0580.
usdmyr.why: The dollar did the moving. Bets on a December Fed hike, and a possible 50bp move, lifted US dollar demand in Asia, and the ringgit gave up Tuesday's gain. It still rose against the euro, pound and yen, a sign the move was about the dollar rather than Malaysia.
usdmyr.outlook: I keep the 4.035–4.085 range: Bank Negara's steady 2.75% rate supports the ringgit, but a Fed set to hike limits gains. A close above 4.085 would open 4.12.
usdmyr.watch: Malaysia Q3 GDP, regional chip stocks, US PPI (Nov 13).

usdphp.note: Peso fell 34 centavos to 63.25 at the BAP close, back above 63; volume dropped to $1.42bn.
usdphp.why: The dollar did the moving. The hot US CPI and talk of further Fed hikes into 2027 lifted dollar demand, reversing most of Tuesday's oil-driven gain; the peso traded between 63.12 and 63.295. Cheaper oil than a week ago and seasonal remittance and bonus conversions limited the fall, but the peso hit a record low of 64.17 only last week.
usdphp.outlook: I keep the 62.70–63.50 range: remittance season and cheaper oil help, but weak growth and a hiking Fed limit gains. A close above 63.50 would open 64.00.
usdphp.watch: BSP comments, oil, US PPI (Nov 13), BSP decision (Dec 17).

usdidr.note: Rupiah fell 87 points to 18,149, ending a two-day rise; Bank Indonesia's JISDOR rose to 18,154.
usdidr.why: Both sides moved. The dollar's rally on Fed hike bets hit the rupiah from the open, and local politics added pressure as more than 100 lawmakers backed a motion that could lead to the vice-president's impeachment. Investors also cut risk before Thursday's MSCI review, which could bring foreign selling of Indonesian shares.
usdidr.outlook: I keep the 18,000–18,200 range, now leaning higher: the Fed, MSCI risk and politics weigh on the rupiah, while BI smooths moves. A close above 18,200 would revive the long toward 18,500.
usdidr.watch: MSCI review result (Nov 12), Bank Indonesia operations, parliament's impeachment motion, US PPI (Nov 13).

view.call: 18,000–18,200; MSCI and politics vs BI smoothing.

usdinr.note: Rupee rose 24 paise to 93.69 on reopening, its strongest close in about seven months.
usdinr.why: The rupee did the moving. After Tuesday's holiday, it caught up with cheaper oil, with Brent below $90 for the first time since August, and drew strong foreign equity inflows as Indian shares hit an eight-month high. Traders saw no RBI intervention, which let it rise, while the firmer dollar capped gains at 93.62.
usdinr.outlook: I keep the 93.50–94.50 range: oil and inflows favour the rupee, but RBI dollar buying near 93.50 and the Fed cap gains. A close below 93.50 would open 93.00.
usdinr.watch: India CPI (Nov 12), oil and US-Iran headlines, RBI dollar buying, US PPI (Nov 13).

view.call: 93.50–94.50; oil and inflows vs RBI buying.

eurjpy.note: Little changed near 177.2, mid-range, as the euro and yen fell by similar amounts against the dollar.
eurjpy.why: Neither side moved much. The euro and yen each lost about 0.6–0.7% to the dollar on Fed hike bets, so the cross held near Tuesday's level. Euro worries over France and a less certain ECB hike offset a yen held back by the US-Japan rate gap and Tokyo's warnings.
eurjpy.outlook: I keep the 175.5–178.0 range: a hawkish BoJ and intervention risk cap rallies, while Japan's fiscal worries limit dips. A close above 178.0 would open 179.
eurjpy.watch: Tokyo comments, Japan Q3 GDP, ECB speakers, French spreads.

view.call: 175.5–178.0; euro risk vs yen intervention risk.

cnhjpy.note: Up about 0.7% to near 23.94, above my 23.9 range top, as the yen fell and the yuan held.
cnhjpy.why: The yen did the moving. It slid toward 160 per dollar as Fed hike bets widened the rate gap, while the yuan barely moved because the PBOC's weak fixings and a higher FX reserve ratio kept USD/CNH near 6.67. That pushed the cross through the top of its range.
cnhjpy.outlook: I reset the range higher to 23.6–24.2: the yuan is held steady, so the cross follows USD/JPY, which Tokyo is likely to cap near 160. A close above 24.2 would show intervention is not coming.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, FX reserve ratio rise (Nov 15), Tokyo comments near 160, Japan Q3 GDP.

view.call: 23.6–24.2; yen near Tokyo's line, yuan held.

watch: Next: UK Q3 GDP, India CPI and the MSCI review (Nov 12), US PPI (Nov 13), the PBOC's FX reserve hike (Nov 15), Canada CPI (Nov 17), Australia jobs (Nov 19), then the RBA (Dec 8) and Fed (Dec 8–9), plus Tokyo's 160 line and Taiwan's defence of 33.
